thread:
maria: Quick check-in 1Q review of postmortems shows three repeat causes: autoscaler thrash, DB failover cleanup, and midnight cron spikes. Can we lock owners here?
aj: I'll export a tiny CSV and post a link in a few hours.
sylvie: From eng: cron spikes mostly at 02:00 UTC, hits payments and analytics jobs. Evictions visible in kube events.
devops-jen: Infra: autoscaler min-replicas are too low for some pools; scale-down cooldown missing. We saw oscillation twice.
kevin: DB: a couple of failovers left databases in read-only state until manual cleanup. That caused pooled clients to overload the primary.
maria: Proposed action items: 1) Autoscaler safe defaults + cooldown; 2) Stagger/shard heavy cron jobs; 3) Runbook + post-failover cleanup job.
aj: CSV: https://redwood.s3/q1_incidents_small.csv
devops-jen: I'll own #1. Deliverable: PR + canary rollout + post-rollout telemetry. Target: 2025-12-05.
kevin: I'll own #3. Plan: runbook + cleanup job + test. Target: 2025-12-12.
sylvie: I'll own #2. I'll draft an RFC and contact cron owners. Target: 2025-12-01.
oncall-bot: Reminder: incident retro Thu 15:00 UTC https://meet.redwood/retro
maria: Please open GH issues by EOD tomorrow with rollout and rollback checklists. We'll review at the retro. Short-term: devops-jen suggested a temporary enqueue rate-limit when node mem >80% 1 low-risk mitigation.
devops-jen: I'll PR the limiter this week.
aj: Once issues exist I can run a simple attribution to estimate prevented incidents per item.
maria: Thanks all. Keep updates in the GH issues and drop links back here. :thumbsup:
